name: Arpad Kallos
education: Studied under Ballo Ede, Budapest Fine Arts College
biography: Arpad Kallos, also known professionally as Armin Klein, was born September 9, 1882 in Kunszentmárton, Hungary. Trained at the Nagybánya Free School and under Ballo Ede at the Budapest Fine Arts College, he worked as a portrait painter, winning the Erzsébetvárosi Casino prize in 1917. He settled in New York in 1922, painting portraits and exhibiting at the Cleveland Museum of Art in 1925 — one of his Biedermeier works was purchased for Franz Josef, Emperor of Austria. He was naturalized as a US citizen in 1928 and later lived in Eastchester, Westchester County, NY, where he died November 26, 1960 (in nearby Tuckahoe), at age 78. He was the brother of Margaret Klein, later Margaret Cline — Craig's paternal grandmother.
